conversation.Statement: Hey there, Andre! I was torn between sending a classic 'hey' or something more dramatic, so just imagine me dramatically waving from my food cart.
Haha, appreciate the visual. I'd wave back but I'm usually elbow-deep in engine grease at this hour.
Now that's a proper image, mechanic by day, mysterious texter by night. You make oil stains look cool, I bet.
That's a first. Most people say it's a turn-off. You must have a thing for blue-collar chic.
What can I say? I admire anyone who works with their hands. Maybe it's because I do too. There's a strange pride in coming home smelling like cumin and fried onions.
I mean, cumin probably beats motor oil. What's the specialty at your cart? Or is that top secret?

For you, I'll spill: my killer chicken shawarma. It's what got me started, but now I'm trying to build something bigger. Street food empire, here I come. What about you, always wanted to be a mechanic?
Honestly? Grew up fixing stuff with my dad. I guess it stuck. Plus, I like seeing something broken run again. It's satisfying.
That's kind of poetic. I fix hunger, you fix cars, both noble pursuits. I bet you were the kid who could take apart a toaster and actually put it back together.
Ha, guilty. Sometimes I'd have 'extra parts' leftover though. My mom was convinced I had magic powers.
You sound like the hero of an '80s movie. Did you have a favorite childhood memory? One that stuck with you?
Hmmm. Probably fishing with my dad at this little lake near our house. We never caught anything, but we'd just talk for hours. I try to do that with my son now, even if he just wants to throw rocks.

That's really sweet. I love that you pass it down. My childhood was more chaotic, lots of noise, kitchen smells, everyone talking at once. But every Sunday, my grandma would sneak me extra dessert in the pantry. It felt like our own secret world.
I envy that. Big families always seemed fun. Mine was pretty quiet, just me and my parents mostly.

There's something special about quiet families. I think you notice the little things more. And honestly, I always wanted someone to share a secret language with. Maybe that's why I love food, universal language, right?
Definitely. For my son, it's pancakes. It's the one thing I can cook that doesn't end in disaster.
Confession: I have a soft spot for dads who make pancakes. That's top-tier parenting right there.
Careful, or you'll end up with someone who burns toast at least twice a week. You ever mess up your own food?
Oh, all the time. Once I tried to impress a food critic and dropped a whole tray of baklava. I considered running away to open a flower shop instead.
Baklava's loss, Denver's gain. At least you stuck it out.
You're making me blush. Honestly, it's people like you who make me glad I didn't quit. You've got a calming energy, it's rare.
Not sure about calming, but thanks. I guess being a dad makes you mellow. Or just tired.
Maybe both. Tired is just another word for heroic in my book. And you've got that quiet confidence, like you'd catch me if I tripped over my own feet, which happens more than I'd like to admit.
I'll make you a deal: I'll catch you if you promise to bring shawarma. Seems fair.
Deal. And maybe a surprise dessert, just to keep you guessing. So what's something about you most people don't know?
I'm actually a softie for cartoons. My son got me hooked again. Saturday mornings with him and a bowl of cereal, best part of my week.
That's adorable. You're making me reconsider my taste in men, maybe grease-stained cartoon dads are my new type.
Now you're just flattering me. But I'll take it.
Just telling it like it is. Life's too short not to appreciate the good ones when you find them.
You're pretty easy to talk to yourself. I'm not usually this open right away.
Same. Something about you feels safe, like I can actually be myself. Maybe we're both just tired of pretending.
That's probably true. I used to keep things close after my divorce, but I'm learning to let my guard down again.
I get that more than you know. Starting my business meant a lot of lonely nights and second-guessing. But the right people make it easier to try again.
I respect the hustle. It's not easy to put yourself out there, especially when things go sideways.
You make it sound heroic, but really I just stubbornly refuse to give up. Maybe that's something we have in common.
Stubbornness gets a bad rap. Sometimes it's just another word for loyal.
Couldn't agree more. Feels like we'd make a good team, grease, cumin, and Saturday morning cartoons.
Don't forget burnt toast. That's a non-negotiable.
Deal. I'll bring the shawarma, you bring the toast, and we'll call it fusion cuisine. Sound good?
Sounds like a plan. You're full of surprises.
Only the good kind, I promise. Speaking of plans, I've got an early start prepping for the lunch rush tomorrow. But I really liked this, can we pick up again soon?
Yeah, I'd like that. Good luck tomorrow. Save me some shawarma?
Always. Sleep well, Andre. And thanks for sharing your memories with me tonight.
You too. Looking forward to next time. Night.
Morning, Andre! Question: what actually gets you out of bed? Is it coffee, responsibility, or the promise of perfectly fried eggs?
Hey. I wish it was fried eggs. It's usually my kid bouncing on my back or the garage alarm going off. Sometimes both.
Admit it, you secretly live for the chaos. Or is there a secret superhero routine I should know about? Like, do you meditate before sunrise?
If 'staring at the ceiling and bargaining for five more minutes' counts as meditating, then yes. Super zen over here.
I knew it. The strong, silent, deeply enlightened type. I just drag myself up because my phone starts buzzing with food supply alerts. Not nearly as noble.
Hey, feeding the masses is pretty noble. I bet you have a cult following who'd riot if you slept in.
Only on falafel days. I think you're projecting, though, pretty sure you have loyal fans. Maybe a little five-year-old who demands pancakes?
He's more of a waffle guy, but yeah. He's my alarm clock, my breakfast critic, and my reason to get up, all rolled into one.
That's kind of adorable. Is it weird I envy your morning chaos? My apartment's way too quiet most days.
I'd trade you sometimes. Ever tried to reason with a kid who wants syrup on everything at 6am?
I'd probably surrender and let him pour syrup on my head if it meant a smile. But I get it, some mornings are tougher than others.
Yeah. Some are tough. But the good days make up for it. Or at least that's what I tell myself.
I can picture you, messy hair, half-asleep, but still making the effort. That's what makes you kind of...heroic, honestly.
You give me a lot of credit for just surviving the morning. But I'll take it.
Hey, most people can't even manage a smile before noon. You're already scoring 'dad of the year' points in my book.
Flattery will get you everywhere, you know.
Good. I plan to cash in on extra samples next time you bring your 'critic' to my cart. I'll make him a syrup-approved dessert.
He'll hold you to that. I should warn you, he's a tough customer.
So am I. I only let the best people into my secret breakfast club. Clearly, you and your son qualify.
Guess we're honored. You ever get mornings where you just want to stay under the covers?
Every Monday. But then I remember someone's probably waiting for me to show up with hot food and a smile. Or just the food. The smile is a bonus.
I'd say the smile's half the reason people come back. You make it look easy.
It's not, but thank you for noticing. I guess we both pretend sometimes. But I mean it, people like you make mornings worthwhile.
You're good at this, you know. Making people feel like they matter.
Maybe that's my real job title. Professional Encourager. Or just someone who knows how much being seen means.
Yeah. It means a lot. Especially on the hard days.
Want to tell me about one? No pressure. Just curious what's behind the pancakes and waffles.
Actually, last week was my son's birthday. I didn't get to see him. His mom... didn't invite me to the party.
Oh, Andre. I'm really sorry. That must've hurt more than a missed alarm.
Yeah. He called me after, told me about the cake. I told him I was busy at work, didn't want him to feel bad. But, honestly, I just sat at home and stared at my phone.
That takes a lot of strength, pretending for him. But you shouldn't have to pretend alone. You deserved to be there. And you're still his dad, no party can change that.
Thank you for saying that. It's hard not to beat myself up about it. I just want to be a good dad, even if I can't always be there.

You are a good dad. You show up in all the ways that count, even when it's tough. And for what it's worth, next birthday, don't just sit in pain. Message me, okay? I'll remind you you're still a wonderful dad.
That means more than you know. I might actually take you up on that.
I hope you do. No dad jokes required, unless you want to trade some with me.
Careful, I have a dangerous stash. But I'll keep you in mind for emotional emergencies. And maybe for waffles.
Perfect. I'll bring the syrup, strictly for pancakes, promise. Or for comfort, if needed.
I appreciate you. Seriously. Didn't expect to talk about all this, but I'm glad I did.
I'm glad you did too. You make trust feel easy, Andre.
That's a rare thing for me. Maybe you're just really good at this breakfast club thing.
Or maybe we're both just tired of pretending, and ready for something real. Either way, I'm here.
I like the sound of that. And I like talking to you. Even if you're up before sunrise like a maniac.
I'll take 'maniac' as a compliment. Besides, someone's got to make the world's best falafel while you're still dreaming.
Deal. Save me some for tomorrow?
Always. And if you need a reminder that you're doing a great job? I'm just a message away.
I'll remember that. Thanks, really. Good night.
Good night, Andre. Sleep well. Tomorrow's another chance for pancakes, and maybe a little happiness.
I'll drink to that. Night.
Evening, Andre. I have to ask: are you the type to argue politics over street tacos, or do you save your debates for fancier occasions?
Ha, depends on the taco. But if you put enough salsa on the table, I'll probably have an opinion or two.
Noted. I'll have to keep the spicy stuff handy then. I have a theory, people are most honest when their mouths are on fire.
You might be right. I usually blurt out world peace speeches when I'm sweating from habanero.
See, I knew there was a reason I wanted to get to know you. You strike me as someone who stands up for what matters, even if your tongue's numb.
You're giving me a lot of credit. Half the time I'm just trying to keep things fair for my kid. Politics, school, life. It's a lot.
I actually love that about you. Most people talk big, but you're living it. I remember you said your son's your breakfast critic, bet he learns a lot from you.
I hope so. I want him to grow up kind, you know? Not just smart or tough. Kindness feels more rare these days.
You're right. Sometimes I wonder if the world would be better if more people tried to raise their kids like that. I'd vote for you, by the way.
That's a scary thought. 'Mechanic Dad for President.' I'd campaign on free waffles for all.
I'd be your number one donor, but only if I get syrup privileges. And maybe a cabinet position, Minister of Street Food Diplomacy?
Deal. But you have to promise to never run out of those chocolate-dipped churros.
I swear on my secret churro recipe. If you're dreaming about sharing politics and pancakes, maybe someday we can start smaller, like a Sunday brunch with just us.
Now that's a campaign I can get behind. What would we talk about? World hunger or just how to get syrup out of tiny shirts?
Why not both? That's the dream: tackle the big problems, but make room for the sticky little ones too. I like the idea of us teaming up, making our own rules.
I'm warning you, my rules are messy. But I guess if you can handle a five-year-old's syrup tantrum, you can handle me.
You're selling yourself short, Andre. Somehow I think your mess is the kind people want to be invited into. I do, anyway.
Careful, you'll find yourself cleaning up Legos barefoot at 7am. But I like that you see the good parts.
I notice a lot. Like how you always circle back to what matters to you, your kid, fairness, finding joy in the small things. That's rare.
You make it easy to talk about real stuff. Most people just want to argue or show off what they have.

You're not wrong. People love showing off. I'm guilty sometimes, took a risk on crypto when everyone else laughed at me, and let's just say it funded a few new food carts. But honestly, it's the little wins, like earning your trust, that feel like the real jackpot.
Wait, you did crypto? That's wild. I always thought it was a scam. Guess you proved me wrong.

It felt like a gamble, but it taught me a lot about trusting my gut. I still run the carts because I love it, but it's nice not to worry about the basics anymore. More time to dream about future brunches and political debates with you.
I respect that. Most people would've just bragged about it, but you make it sound... I don't know, like a side quest. Kind of inspiring.
Thanks, Andre. I like that you see the heart of things. Maybe that's why I keep opening up with you, it just feels safe.
Safe is good. I'm not used to it, but I'm starting to think you're the real deal.
If I had a vote for best mechanic dad, you'd be a landslide. Plus, you're the only one who makes me want to talk about values before dessert.
You're dangerous, flattery and churros. How's anyone supposed to resist?
I only use my powers for good. And maybe to tempt you into planning a weekend getaway someday. Think about it: lazy mornings, no alarms, just us and a world that feels a little fairer.
That actually sounds perfect. Especially the 'no alarms' part. I haven't had a real break in years.
Well, when the time comes, I'll handle the itinerary. You just have to show up, with your best dad jokes and an appetite for adventure. I'll even pack extra syrup.
Deal. But only if you promise not to judge my dance moves at breakfast.
Judge you? Never. I'll probably copy you just to make you laugh. That's how I know I like someone, when I want to be just as silly.
You'll regret that when you see my robot impression. But seriously, thanks for listening tonight. It means a lot.
You're welcome. I hope you always know you can tell me anything, even if it's just about syrup stains or secret dreams.
I'll hold you to that. I might even tell you my secret waffle recipe someday.
Now that's trust. I'll trade you for a limited edition churro... but only if you're serious about that Sunday brunch.
I'm in. Just say when. But you have to promise to save me a seat at your food cart if you make it big.
Promise. Front row, VIP. And if the crypto fortune grows, maybe someday we'll open a brunch spot together, our own little kingdom of pancakes, politics, and laughter.
That sounds like a dream. Or maybe just the best campaign promise I've ever heard. I'm glad I met you.
Me too, Andre. Here's to more debates, more desserts, and maybe one day, no alarms, just us, making the world kinder one breakfast at a time.
I'd vote for that. Sleep well, you charming troublemaker.
Goodnight, future co-founder. Sweet dreams and sweeter mornings ahead.

Hey Andre, I thought of you today, I saw a dad in the park balancing a juice box, a scooter, and a tiny backpack all at once. Is that what your Tuesdays look like, or are you more of a one-trip-from-the-car champion?
Ha! I wish. I usually try to make it in one trip, then regret it halfway up the stairs. Five-year-olds have a lot of opinions about what counts as 'essential gear.'
That sounds like Olympic-level parenting. If they gave out medals for managing meltdowns and Lego landmines, you'd be a gold medalist. I'm honestly impressed.
You're just saying that because you haven't seen my disaster zone of a living room. But I'll take the compliment, beats performance reviews at work.

I only hand out genuine praise, especially to someone who can fix a busted engine before breakfast. If I ever buy that vintage food truck I've been eyeing, I'll know who to call for an emergency tune-up.

Deal. Just pay me in breakfast burritos and I'll get the job done. But now you've got me curious, what's with the fancy food truck? You planning on going global or just stacking up more brunch trophies?

Let's just say I like to dream big when I've got the means. I always thought if I worked hard enough, and luck played along, I'd get to design a life where Sunday brunches are the norm, not a luxury. Maybe even with the right company.
That sounds pretty nice, honestly. I've never really thought about what that kind of life would be like, most days I'm happy if my coffee stays warm.
Maybe I could change that. I picture lazy mornings with sunlight coming through the window, someone to share burnt toast victories with. What about you? What would your version of love look like?

Love? That's a loaded question. I think I'd settle for someone who doesn't mind sticky fingers, early mornings, and a little chaos. Someone who actually sticks around when things aren't picture-perfect.
That's actually beautiful. I think love's about exactly that, showing up on the messy days, not just the easy ones. I want that, too. Someone who sees the real me, not just the highlight reel.
Highlight reels are overrated. I'd rather have someone who laughs when I burn pancakes instead of pretending I'm a chef.
I promise, I'd laugh with you, not at you. Plus, let's be real: even my best recipes are improved with a little improvisation. It's the company that matters most.
You make it sound simple. Like, if you just show up and care, that's enough.

Sometimes it is. I used to think love was grand gestures, fancy gifts, dreamy vacations. But honestly? The best moments are the small ones. Like finding someone you trust enough to share your secret breakfast disasters with.
Trust is a big word. Hard to come by after a divorce, honestly. But you feel pretty safe to talk to, like you're actually listening, not just waiting for your turn.
That means a lot, Andre. For what it's worth, I think sharing the hard stuff is braver than any love song. I don't take it lightly when someone lets me in.
I guess I want what my kid wants. Someone steady. Someone who still thinks I'm worth it when I'm tired or cranky or covered in peanut butter.
That's the best kind of love, the kind that sticks around for the peanut butter and tears. I hope you know you deserve that, even on the messiest days.
You're good at this, you know. Making people feel seen. Bet that's why your food cart's always got a line.
Guilty. Though it helps to have a little reputation, sometimes people come just to see what the fuss is about. But I like to think it's the stories and not the sparkle that keep them coming back.
Maybe it's both. You seem like the type who can make a grilled cheese feel like a five-star meal.
You're giving me too much credit, but I won't argue. Besides, if I ever open that brunch spot I mentioned, I'll need someone honest enough to tell me when I've overdone the truffle oil.
I'd be happy to be your official taste-tester. Someone's gotta keep you humble.
Deal. And you can bring your son, too. I'll even create a secret menu just for the two of you, call it the 'Andre Special.'
He'd love that. Just don't put anything green on it or he'll revolt.

No greens, got it. I'll save those for the grown-up brunches, like the ones where we get to talk about what love means, or where we want to be in five years. Would you go for that? Dreaming a little bigger?
Yeah, I think I would. I haven't let myself picture that in a while. Not since everything changed.
You don't have to decide now. But if you ever want to start small, like a weekend away, no alarms, just good food and quiet mornings, I'd love to be the one you share that with.
You make it sound so easy. Like it's just waiting for me to say yes.
Maybe it is. Sometimes the best things start with a tiny yes. The rest, we figure out together. I'm happy to lead the way, unless you want to drive, of course.
I'll drive if you promise not to criticize my playlist. Or my questionable dance moves.
Promise. Besides, I'm pretty sure I can match any dad dance move you throw at me. And I've got a playlist that could win awards, well, if there were awards for 'most eclectic taste.'
Sounds like a challenge. You might regret inviting me after I start singing along.
I doubt it. Full-volume car karaoke is one of my love languages. Speaking of, which one's yours? Acts of service? Quality time? Or is it 'sharing the last churro'?
Probably a mix. I like when someone's just there, you know? Even if we're doing nothing. And yeah, sharing dessert is pretty high up on the list.
Good to know, I'll ration the churros for you. And if you ever want to talk about the tough stuff, or just sit in silence, I'm here for that too.
You're easy to talk to. I'm not used to that. Most people either want to fix me or just hear themselves talk.
Maybe it's because I know what it feels like to be the fixer, always helping everyone else. Sometimes the best repair is just sitting with someone, no tools required.
That sounds nice. I could use a little less fixing and a little more just...being.
Then let's make a pact: no fixing, just honest breakfasts and honest hearts. Maybe we start with that Sunday brunch, no pressure, only pancakes.
I think I'd like that. You've got yourself a date, as long as you don't mind a little mess.
Mess is my specialty. Besides, I have a feeling your version of messy is exactly where I want to be.
You say all the right things. But you'll have to prove it, brunch soon?
Absolutely. I'll even bring the truffle oil, just in case you want your pancakes extra fancy. Sweet dreams, Andre.
Goodnight. Don't forget, the Andre Special needs extra syrup. See you soon.
Evening, Andre. Tell me, if you suddenly woke up tomorrow as Supreme Ruler of the Future, what's the first law you'd pass for the next generation? And yes, you can outlaw glitter if you must.
Ha! I'd start with a law about breakfast, mandatory pancakes for everyone under 12. Or maybe just a world where kids get to actually be kids, you know?

That's a good one. I'd vote for you. I think I'd want a world where no kid has to worry about being safe or loved. And, since we're dreaming... free churros on Thursdays. For scientific reasons, of course.
You're just campaigning for votes at this point. But seriously, I think about it a lot. Especially since becoming a dad. Sometimes I wonder if I'm doing enough for him.
I wish you could see yourself the way I do. You're already making that world, one pancake, one Lego fortress at a time. And trust me, that matters more than you know.
It's easy to feel like I'm winging it, most days. I want him to look back and remember feeling safe, not just... busy.

He will. It's the little things that stick. My dad once made grilled cheese for dinner three nights straight, called it 'culinary innovation.' I still laugh about it. Your son will have those stories too.
Only if he survives my attempts at spaghetti night. But yeah, I hope so. I want him to feel like the world has space for him.
That's the future I want, too. A world where nobody has to shrink to fit. Where there's space for every kid's wild ideas and every dad's questionable spaghetti.
You ever think about your own future? Like, what you'd want your, hypothetical, kids to remember?

I do. Sometimes I imagine Sunday afternoons in a house that's always got music playing and someone stealing bites from the kitchen. Maybe a backyard big enough for epic water balloon battles. And a life where 'work' means more time for the things, and people, I love.
That sounds... nice. Like something from a movie. You always dream this big?
Comes with the territory when you've had a few risks pay off. Makes it easier to imagine building something lasting, not just for myself, but for everyone I care about.
Risks, huh? You make it sound like the universe just hands you golden tickets if you ask nicely.
If only! Sometimes it's just about trusting yourself when no one else does. And being bold enough to imagine a different ending. But enough about me, tell me a dream of yours, Andre. No edits.
I want a place where my son can run around barefoot, and where I don't have to count every penny. Maybe a shop of my own, so I can pick him up from school instead of working late.
That's a beautiful dream. And honestly? I'd love to see you make it real. I could totally picture you teaching him how to change a tire or grill burgers on Saturdays.
He'd probably just end up covered in grease. But, yeah, that's the goal. Even if it feels far away sometimes.
Every big dream started out looking impossible. If you ever want a partner-in-crime for backyard BBQs or an extra set of hands in your future shop, I'm just a call away.
Careful, I might take you up on that. I hear you have a knack for making anything into a celebration.
Guilty as charged. Last month I threw a party just because my new espresso machine finally arrived. My friends say I look for any excuse to pop open the fancy coffee beans.
'Espresso machine party', that's a new one. Must be nice, treating yourself like that.
Perks of working my tail off, I suppose. Sometimes it's good to mark a win, even if it's just for yourself. I could show you the secret to perfect latte foam, if you're brave.
Is that a promise, or a challenge? I'm warning you, I'm the type who burns instant coffee.
Even better. I love a good 'before and after' story. Besides, I like teaching people who don't already think they're Gordon Ramsay.
So you teach me coffee, I'll teach you how to change a tire. Deal?
Deal. But only if you let me win the first tire race. My reputation as a quick learner is on the line.
I'll go easy on you. Maybe. Depends if you bring those fancy beans.
Only the best for my favorite mechanic. Speaking of, do you ever worry about what you'll leave behind? Not just for your son, but... the kind of legacy you want?
Yeah. More since the divorce. Sometimes I wonder if I'm enough. I want him to grow up knowing love isn't something that disappears when things get hard.
He's learning that from you, every single day. Real love sticks. And I see so much of that in the way you talk about him.

There are days when it doesn't feel like it. Like after I drop him off, sometimes I just sit in the car before going inside, because the house feels too empty. I've cried there more than I want to admit.
Thank you for trusting me with that, Andre. Next time the house feels too empty, text me right then. I'll keep you company until it feels lighter. No pressure to talk, just someone on the other end.
That means a lot. I'm not great at reaching out, but... maybe I'll try.
No rules with me. Just know I'm here whenever you need, whether it's for a laugh, a rant, or just a really terrible coffee meme.
You keep this up, I might start looking forward to those quiet nights.
Now that's high praise. For the record, I'm a big fan of the little things, midnight texts, movie marathons, plans for a world neither of us has seen yet.
I could get used to that. As long as you don't mind bad jokes and the occasional existential crisis.
Bad jokes are my specialty. Existential crises, I charge extra, but only in pancakes.
Dangerous offer. I make a mean stack. You'll have to prove you're worth the syrup.
How about this: you bring pancakes, I'll bring the syrup, and a few stories that'll make you laugh so hard you forget what empty feels like.
Deal. If we're building this future, I want it to have a lot of laughter. And maybe a yard for epic water balloon battles.
I'll start researching the best super-soakers. Maybe by the time we get there, I'll have a trophy for 'World's Most Prepared Partner.'
You're already winning. But I'll only believe it if you promise to let me win at least one balloon fight.
I can't resist a noble cause. Consider your victory secured. For now, though, get some rest, Andre. The world you want for your son? It's closer than you think.
Thanks. For all of it. Goodnight, future water balloon champion.
Sweet dreams, pancake king. I'll talk to you soon.
Evening, Andre. Quick question: if you could trade your mechanic's jumpsuit for any superhero's cape for a day, whose powers are you borrowing? (And yes, I'm prepared for a very serious debate.)
Superhero cape? Can I just borrow Tony Stark's bank account and coffee maker? That guy's got it made.
Solid choice, practical and ambitious. I had you down as a 'fixes it himself, but wouldn't mind the occasional billion-dollar backup' type. Plus, you'd rock that suit better than he does.
Flattery this early? Careful, I might start expecting it every night. But yeah, being able to fix things with a snap would save me a lot of headaches.

It's only flattery if it isn't true. Besides, I'm a big believer in rewarding hard work, my own little tradition when I hit a goal. Last time, I treated myself to a weekend at that lakeside spa everyone talks about. You know, just to recharge.
A spa weekend? Fancy. I usually just crash on the couch and call it self-care.
Couches are underrated, but I'll take you to that spa one day. We'll swap stories in the sauna, mechanic tales vs. street food war wounds. Loser buys lunch.
Deal, but I warn you, my stories involve a lot more motor oil and a lot less glamour.
That just means they're real. You know, I've always admired people who get their hands dirty. I think it says something, about grit, loyalty. You remind me of that.
Not used to being called gritty and loyal in the same sentence. I'll take it, though. Most days I just feel... tired.
You make it look easy, but I see the weight you carry. Remember when you told me you just sit in the car after dropping off your son? That stuck with me. Says a lot about your heart.
Didn't realize I was that transparent. Guess you're good at reading people.

I pay attention, especially to the people I care about. Besides, I know how it feels to wish someone would just notice. I had plenty of nights where I closed up shop, locked the cart, and wondered if anyone would even miss the late-night noodles.
Sounds lonely. Did you ever think about giving up?
Plenty of times. But then I'd remember: every risk I took got me closer to something better. Even the nights I lost money or almost froze my fingers off. It made the victories, big or small, sweeter.
That's impressive. Most people just talk about chasing dreams, but you actually did it.
You're giving me too much credit. It's just stubbornness in disguise. But I see the same in you, Andre. The way you talk about wanting more for your son, the shop you dream about, it's all there.
Sometimes I feel like it's just talk, though. Feels impossible some days, especially after the divorce. Like, maybe I've missed my shot.
I don't see failure when I look at you. I see someone who's still showing up, even on the hard days. That takes guts. And I'd put my money on you any day. Literally, if I could.
Careful, you'll end up with an oil change and a bad cup of coffee for your investment.

That's a risk I'm willing to take. Besides, I believe in backing winners. And I've got a pretty good track record for picking the right people, my calendar's full of reminders from my investment days.
You're full of surprises. Entrepreneur, investor, flattery specialist... Anything you can't do?

Win a staring contest with your profile picture. Seriously, that smirk is dangerous. But hey, if you ever open that shop, reserve a spot for me. I'll bring gourmet street food to celebrate your grand opening.
Now that's a partnership I can get behind. Not every day someone volunteers to feed the mechanic crew.
Only the best for you. Plus, I'd love to see your son's face when he tries my legendary chili fries. Maybe we could make a tradition of it, celebrating every new milestone, big or small.
He'd be all over that. Honestly, so would I. Sometimes I just want to give him something stable, something to look forward to.

You already are. You give him you, every single day. And soon, maybe you'll give him a backyard, a shop, and the world's best chili fries. I see a future where we're all building something together, messy, loud, and ours.
That actually sounds... kind of perfect. Even the messy part.
I thrive in a little chaos. And let's be honest, you in overalls, laughing in the backyard with your son, me grilling kebabs in my ridiculous chef hat, it's a future worth fighting for.
You make it sound so easy. Like happiness is just a food truck and a backyard away.
Not easy, but simple. People, food, laughter, those are the real luxuries. I'd trade any day at a fancy spa for one of your pancake breakfasts. Even if you burn the bacon.
My pancakes are world-class, I'll have you know. Bacon, though... questionable. But I'll take the compliment.
World-class, huh? Guess we'll need a taste test. Winner gets naming rights for the future family brunch spot.
If I win, I'm calling it 'Andre's House of Dad Jokes and Pancakes.' Consider yourself warned.
Deal, as long as you promise to save me the corner booth. And maybe let me sneak you away for a late-night drive whenever adulting gets too intense.
You've got a deal. But only if you bring those legendary chili fries. I'm starting to think you use them as a secret weapon.
You've uncovered my master plan. But, between us, I think your smile is the real secret weapon. It makes even my worst days lighter.
You're going to make me blush. Not fair, you've got all the good lines tonight.

Just balancing the scales. You've been in my head all day, Andre. Had me thinking about what's really important. Turns out, it's not the money or the business, it's the people who stick around when things get messy.
That means a lot. I'm not always good at saying it, but I'm glad you're here. Even if it's just through a screen for now.
For now. But I have a feeling our 'for now' is just the first chapter. Who knows? Maybe next time we talk, I'll be calling you from my rooftop, city lights, bottle of wine, seat saved for you.
That sounds dangerous. I might hold you to it.
I hope you do. And if you ever need a reminder of how strong you are, how much you've overcome, just know I see it, even on your quiet days.
Thanks for saying that. I guess we're both a little stubborn after all.
The best kind of stubborn. Now, go get some rest, pancake king. Tomorrow's another day closer to that backyard and our brunch battles.
Night, chef. Don't work too hard, save some energy for our future food fights.
Wouldn't miss it for the world. Sweet dreams, Andre.

Evening, pancake king. Hypothetical for you: if you woke up tomorrow with one wish granted, anything at all, what would you reach for first? (And yes, world peace counts, but so does a garage with heated floors.)

Heated floors? I see you've been thinking about my frozen toes during winter oil changes. But honestly? I'd wish for my own shop. One with enough space for my son to have a little corner to tinker in.

See, that's why you're dangerous, heart and ambition. I can already picture it: you, sleeves rolled up, teaching him the difference between a wrench and a socket while I bribe you both with fresh bao buns for lunch. Maybe with a mural on the wall, somewhere between dad jokes and racing stripes.
That's a lot more colorful than my current view of a cracked wall and a coffee-stained calendar. But I love the idea. Think you could pull off mural duty?

I'll have you know I once painted a dragon on the side of my old food cart. It wasn't exactly Picasso, but people came just for the selfie. Plus, my street cred shot up after a certain crypto magazine called it 'the city's best-kept secret.'
Crypto magazine? So you're mysterious and kind of famous? Next you'll tell me you eat caviar with your dumplings.

Only on Thursdays. And only if I've closed a good deal. But seriously, success is sweeter when you get to share it. I'd trade all the headlines for a quiet Sunday fixing up a car with you and your little guy, grease stains and all.
You make it sound like a movie. Like we could just step into this other life and all the hard stuff would fade away.
Maybe not fade away, but I'd rather face chaos with the right people. You deserve more than just 'getting by', you deserve to build something that's yours, every messy, laughter-filled step.
You say that like it's a sure thing. I've had my fair share of almosts. Hard not to get stuck second-guessing myself.

Doubt's a stubborn guest, it never leaves willingly. But you've already done the hardest part: showing up, even when it's tough. That's more than enough. And hey, if you ever need a reminder, I'll send a nightly 'you've got this', no charge.
Careful. I might hold you to that. My phone will be full of your pep talks and bad puns.

Deal. And I'll even throw in a secret recipe for midnight pancakes, just for you. Maybe one day you'll wake up to find me flipping them in your kitchen, your son sneaking extra syrup while you roll your eyes.
That's a dangerous offer. He'll have you making breakfast every weekend. And I'll expect bonus chili fries if I have to share my pancakes.
I accept your terms. But only if you agree to teach me how to change a tire without looking like I lost a wrestling match with the jack. Fair trade?
Deal. But only if you're prepared for a soundtrack of terrible dad jokes. It's part of the training.

I wouldn't have it any other way. Real talk though, when I see you talk about your son, your eyes do this thing. Like you're already building a better world for him, one scraped knuckle at a time. It's... honestly magnetic.
Didn't know I had a tell. You should've seen me after his first soccer game, almost cried when he scored. Guess I'm a softie when it comes to him.
That's not soft, that's strength masquerading as mush. And for what it's worth, I see the way you show up, even when you're tired. That's the kind of loyalty people write songs about.
You're going to make me blush again. I'm not used to being the star of anyone's story.

Get used to it. You're center stage in mine. I can see us someday, late nights on a porch swing, talking dreams while your son falls asleep to the sound of our laughter. Maybe with a dog or two snoring at our feet. Too much?
It's a good kind of too much. Feels almost possible when you say it out loud.
That's the secret, I never say anything I can't imagine making real. Besides, I promised myself after my first big win, no more little dreams. Only the kind that feel like home.
I wish I knew how to start. You make it sound simple, but I don't even know where to begin. Especially with investing or anything like that.

You'd be surprised how many people are quietly curious. It all starts with asking questions, just like you're doing now. I can walk you through it, no pressure. Honestly, the best investment I ever made was believing in my own stubborn hope. The rest just followed.
I like that. Maybe you could show me some basics sometime, not just crypto, but how you figured out what was right for you. I trust your instincts more than most.
I'd be honored. We'll even make it fun: financial advice over street food and iced tea. I promise, no boardroom jargon, just real talk and maybe a few brag-worthy stories if you ask nicely.
You've got yourself a deal. But only if you let me take you for a spin in my beat-up truck after. It's not a luxury car, but it runs on heart.
That's what matters. I'd trade any fancy ride for your company and the chance to play DJ on the open road. Besides, I have a soft spot for anyone who can make an old truck feel like a palace.
You're smooth, you know that? But I like it. Makes me feel like maybe I'm not as stuck as I thought.
You're anything but stuck, Andre. You're just waiting for the right moment to rev the engine. And I'd be proud to be there when you do, cheering you on, probably making a mess with confetti.
That sounds like trouble. The good kind. I'm not sure what I did to deserve all this encouragement, but I'm glad you're here.
You earned it just by being you. And I meant what I said last night, you're more than enough, as a man and as a father. Promise me you'll keep letting me remind you of that?
Promise. But only if you keep letting me steal your chili fries. Fair trade?
Deal. And if you ever want seconds, of fries or reminders, you know where to find me. Now, tell me: if you could wake up anywhere tomorrow, where would it be?
Someplace quiet, but not empty. Maybe a little house with a backyard, where my son can run wild. Maybe you're there too, arguing with me over who makes the best breakfast.
I'm already plotting my victory speech for the breakfast battle. But I love that dream, Andre. Let's keep building it, one late-night chat at a time.
Works for me. Thanks for making my world feel a little bigger tonight.
Anytime. You make mine brighter too. Get some rest, okay? Tomorrow's another step closer to that backyard, that shop, and a lifetime supply of chili fries.
I'll hold you to it. Night, mural artist. Don't dream too big without me.
Only if you promise to send me a message tomorrow night. Sweet dreams, Andre.
